first_impression.reaction: I'm on the train, I typed 'wedding rsvp website' and the first thing I get is 'the quiet workhorse of a destination wedding' and an aunt in Perth. Nice line, but I wasn't asking about destination weddings. The second paragraph saves it because it tells me there are five kinds and a checklist, and the Key takeaways are right under it. I'd scroll straight to those, then the comparison table.

journey.quote: A wedding RSVP website is the quiet workhorse of a destination wedding.
journey.reaction: Bit of a scene-setter before the answer. I don't need the aunt and the colleague. Tell me what it is in one line and I'm happy.

journey.quote: This guide compares the five kinds of RSVP website, the questions worth asking before you pay for anything, and the details that matter when guests are crossing oceans to be there.
journey.reaction: Okay, this is the line that keeps me. Five kinds, and what to check before paying. I'd like to know what the five are right here, though, without scrolling.

journey.quote: Before paying for an upgrade, check guest and event limits, custom questions, exports, password protection and whether guests see the tool's branding or ads.
journey.reaction: Useful. That's a checklist I can actually use when I open the sign-up pages. Screenshot-worthy.

journey.quote: Print the RSVP web address beside any QR code and test-scan the printed proof before the full print run.

journey.section: The five kinds of wedding RSVP website compared
journey.quote: There is no single right tool, only the right kind for your guest list, judged on what a destination weekend asks of it.
journey.reaction: Fine, but I was half expecting names. Every other result gives me a list of actual sites. Here I get categories. The table is clear though, and I can work out which kind I am.

journey.section: The five kinds of wedding RSVP website compared
journey.quote: Wonderland Studio, our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs, sits in this group.
journey.reaction: At least they say it's theirs instead of pretending to be neutral. I respect that. Doesn't tell me if it costs anything though.

journey.section: What changes between paid tiers and those at no cost
journey.quote: What changes between paid tiers and those at no cost
journey.reaction: Awkward heading. I'm scanning for 'free' and this reads oddly. The list under it is good, though.

journey.section: What changes between paid tiers and those at no cost
journey.quote: Plans change often, so run the same questions on any tool you are considering.
journey.reaction: So no prices. 'Just tell me how much it costs.' I get why they can't, but I'm leaving this section without a number.

journey.section: Guest privacy and who can see the site
journey.quote: As general information as at November 2026, and not legal advice: personal information includes information or an opinion that could identify an individual, depending on whether that person is identifiable in the circumstances.
journey.reaction: Dated, which I like, so I know it's current. But this is heavy for a phone on the train and it's Australian law. I'd skim past to the 'password-protect the site' bit.

journey.section: Guest privacy and who can see the site
journey.quote: Whatever the law asks, good manners ask more: password-protect the site, share the list only with the suppliers who need it, and delete what you no longer need after the wedding.
journey.reaction: This is the bit I actually needed from that section. Clear.

journey.section: What to ask on your RSVP form
journey.quote: Every extra question is a reason to put the reply off.
journey.reaction: Good, short list, exactly the kind of thing I'd copy.

journey.quote: Yes, on a no-cost tier. Check guest and event limits, custom questions, export, branding and ads before you commit.
journey.reaction: Direct answer to the thing I really wanted to know. FAQ is tight and scannable.

unanswered_questions: Which actual RSVP websites fit each of the five kinds? (I understand the page doesn't name any, but I'll have to Google again.)
Does Wonderland Studio cost anything, or can I use it without paying?
Roughly what does a paid tier cost, even as a range?
When was this page last updated? Only the privacy section is dated.

turn_offs_found.quote: A wedding RSVP website is the quiet workhorse of a destination wedding. It is where your aunt in Perth, your school friends in London and your colleague in Singapore all tell you the same things: whether they are coming, which nights they will be there, what they eat and when their flight lands.
turn_offs_found.why: First 50 words are mood, not answer, and assume a destination wedding I never searched for.

turn_offs_found.quote: What changes between paid tiers and those at no cost
turn_offs_found.why: Heading doesn't match how I'd phrase it. I'm scanning for free versus paid.

would_share_with: My fiance, for the 'What to ask on your RSVP form' list and the tier checklist

cta_reaction.quote: Weighing several events, room blocks and a guest list across time zones? Talk to our [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-rsvp-website&utm_content=primary) team about the weekend you have in mind.
cta_reaction.why: I came for an RSVP tool, not a planner. I don't know this brand yet. I might tap the Wonderland Studio link to see if it's free, and I'd bookmark the page, but I'm not talking to a concierge today.

top_3_changes: Answer the query in the first line. OLD: "A wedding RSVP website is the quiet workhorse of a destination wedding. It is where" NEW: "A wedding RSVP website is a page or form where guests reply to your invitation online, and it is the quiet workhorse of a destination wedding. It is where"

Name the five kinds in the intro so I can see the answer without scrolling. OLD: "This guide compares the five kinds of RSVP website, the questions worth asking" NEW: "This guide compares the five kinds of RSVP website (all-in-one wedding websites, standalone RSVP tools, invitation platforms, planning apps and a DIY form plus spreadsheet), the questions worth asking"
Make the tier heading match how people search. OLD: "## What changes between paid tiers and those at no cost" NEW: "## No-cost or paid: what changes between tiers"

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft

No invented brand facts; Wonderland Studio cost and platform names logged as unanswered, not assumed
Suggested edits use exact old/new strings, name no platforms, add no fees, commissions or supplier claims
HTML comments and image slots treated as invisible

open_questions.question: This persona will notice that no platforms are named and no Wonderland Studio price is given. Both are deliberate brand limits, so I logged them as unanswered rather than as changes. Confirm no action is expected.

Search intent is generic (not specifically a destination wedding), per the persona card.
